description.p: Home Cinema plays the movies, shows and music of your own Jellyfin server on a Phosh phone and on the desktop.

ul.li: Continue watching, next episodes and the newest items of every library
Resume where you stopped; progress is kept on the server
At home it talks to the server directly, elsewhere through its public address
Works with servers that require a client certificate
The server converts videos the phone can't play

description.p: Home Cinema is an independent project and not affiliated with the Jellyfin project.

ul.li: Choose the audio track and subtitles while watching; text subtitles show over the video and picture subtitles are burned in by the server.
Autoplay of the next episode can be turned off in the preferences and in the player's new Playback Settings.
The player shows when the video ends, skips intros and credits that the server has marked, and goes on to the next episode with a button or after a short countdown.
Videos pause when the screen turns off; a new preference keeps them playing.
Double tap the left or right side of a video to skip back or forward, use the large buttons in the middle, or turn the video to landscape with the new rotate button.
Servers behind a reverse proxy with its own login (such as Pangolin, Authelia or Authentik) work: Ephyra shows the proxy's login page and keeps the session.
Choose a light or dark style in the preferences, or follow the system style, which Ephyra now does by default.
While the server converts a video, the player says “Converting on the server…”.
The app is now called Home Cinema.
Addresses typed without http:// or https:// now always use https://.
Picture subtitles (PGS, DVD) are no longer turned on by themselves, because the server has to convert the whole video for them; they can still be chosen and are marked “converted on the server”.
When a video can’t be played, the error page shows a short reason and a details line with the file’s format and the server’s answer that you can copy into a bug report.
Blu-ray remuxes with TrueHD or DTS audio now play directly instead of being converted on the server.
The play, back and forward buttons in the middle of a video work again.
Japanese, Chinese and Korean titles, descriptions and subtitles are shown instead of empty boxes.
When a video can’t be played, Ephyra says whether your Jellyfin user may have videos converted, and “Convert on the Server” now converts the whole video.
Videos and music now play in the app on the phone; before, playback stopped with “Failed to pause”.
Leaving the home Wi-Fi while Ephyra runs now switches to the remote address right away, and a playing video continues through it.
Ephyra now always tells the server to stop converting a video when you leave the player, switch tracks or retry, also while the video is still loading, so no conversions keep running on the server.
Choosing another subtitle or audio track no longer jumps back to the previous choice when the server has to prepare the video again.
The audio and subtitle choice is no longer covered by the timeline.

description.p: First version: sign in to a Jellyfin server, browse the libraries and play movies, episodes and music.
